source_lock.appendix: Appendix A.1 Consistency of Floral Measurements

measurement_protocol.between_individual_validation: three individuals measured the same subset of herbarium specimens
measurement_protocol.within_individual_validation: the same individual repeated measurements on the same subset roughly one month later
measurement_protocol.source_interpretation_of_slope: accuracy/scale agreement; slope 1 denotes exact proportional agreement

equal_error_proxy_assumptions: both replicate measurements equal the same latent trait plus independent homoscedastic zero-mean error
replicate measurements share the same scale with no systematic proportional or additive bias
the external herbarium measurement process transfers to the predictor scale and source mixture used in the Southwest Pacific analysis
estimand_assessment.reason: Several repeat/inter-observer slopes differ materially from 1 and intercepts are nonzero; the validation is from a different study and trait-combination protocol. R-squared therefore demonstrates empirical consistency but does not identify the reliability ratio required by the classical x-error correction.

claim_boundary: The source-locked thesis supplies genuine repeated-measurement evidence and shows high floral measurement consistency. Under an explicitly hypothetical equal-error/no-bias model, sqrt(R-squared) proxies exceed the current Southwest Pacific reliability thresholds. Because the source does not establish those assumptions and some repeat slopes depart from one, the proxies are sensitivity evidence only and must not be substituted for an observed reliability coefficient.
